newsitem.title: USA: China says delay in joining WTO hurts world trade.
newsitem.headline: China says delay in joining WTO hurts world trade.

text.p: In a clear reference to the U.S. government, China on Tuesday said the delay by "certain parties" in letting it join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) was hurting the development of world trade.
The United States is pressing its fifth largest trading partner to open up its markets to imports as a condition for its membership of the trade body.

"The unreasonable demands of certain contracting parties have delayed China's accession to the WTO...bringing unfavourable consequences for the healthy development of world trade," the head of the People's Bank of China, Dai Xianglong, told the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank.

The central banker criticised the frequent use of trade sanctions by some industrial countries and said it was vital for them to reduce non-trade barriers and give greater access to developing countries.
Dai said China has already stated that it is prepared to take on the obligations of WTO membership.
He also urged Western nations to improve their economic peformance.

Industrial nations should strengthen their budgetary positions, push ahead with labour market reform and so create favourable conditions for lower interest rates and minimise uncertainty in the world economy, he added.

Pointing to the Chinese economy, he said he was well aware of the challenges it faced, especially in making state firms more efficient, further strengthening its own fiscal postion and improving the quality of commercial bank loans.
"The solution to these problems lies in deepening the reform and maintaining appropriately tight monetary and fiscal policies,' Dai said.
